The more interesting part is spelling. A one-syllable verb ending in one vowel plus one consonant usually doubles that consonant (stop becomes stopped). A verb ending in a consonant plus y changes y to -ied (carry becomes carried). A verb ending in e just takes -d (smile becomes smiled).
